title: Roth IRA vs Roth 401(k): the gap
audience: High earners in jobs with 401(k) plans who think they've maxed their Roth
thesis: The Roth IRA is $7,500. The Roth 401(k) is $24,500. Most people miss the gap.

concepts.label: The limit gap
concepts.body: The 2026 Roth IRA limit is $7,500 — your own money, your own brokerage. The 2026 Roth 401(k) limit is $24,500 — same tax treatment, $17,000 more room.

concepts.label: Why the Roth 401(k) has no income phaseout
concepts.body: Unlike the Roth IRA, the Roth 401(k) has no income phaseout. Earn $400,000, $800,000, more — you can still fund it. The phaseout only applies to IRAs.

concepts.label: Mega backdoor angle
concepts.body: The Roth 401(k) is also the only path to the mega backdoor Roth: after-tax 401(k) contributions plus in-plan conversions can push annual Roth savings above $70,000.
